commit.subject: refactor(steme): migrate the rulepack parser to zod, behavior-preserving
commit.body:
Replace parse-rulepack.ts's hand-rolled validation with a Zod core ahead of
the manifest validator (next phase), so apps/steme carries one validation
library, not two styles. Adds zod pinned to the workspace's existing
^3.25.64. No observable change: the 30-case parser test file passes
unmodified, same accepted/rejected rulepacks, same ConfigError fields.

phases.title: Migrate the rulepack parser to Zod, behavior-preserving

commit.subject: feat(steme): require and validate the unit manifest in the audit preflight
commit.body:
steme audit (and both baseline commands via the shared preflight) now reads
<app-path>/steme.package.json right after the target check: missing,
structurally invalid, containment-violating, or rulepack-undeclared-concept
manifests are cannot-run (exit 2) with config-error messages, ahead of the
rulepack step, first-failing-step precedence unchanged. Validation is a Zod
mirror of schemas/steme.package.schema.json, kept divergence-free by a
parity test that runs shared fixtures through both validators.
apps/steme and packages/example-utility declare core.composition and
core.capabilities so every unit's audit gate stays green; the E2E temp
units now carry the sandbox manifest. Resolution itself still uses the
hardcoded maps — replaced next commit.

phases.title: The manifest becomes a required, validated audit input

commit.subject: feat(steme): resolve scope and concept bindings from the unit manifest
commit.body:
evaluateRules now takes a resolver built from the audited unit's
steme.package.json; the hardcoded scope-map.ts/concept-map.ts are deleted
with no fallback. A scope key absent from the manifest is vacuous (matches
nothing, not an error); two scope globs matching one file is a config
error naming the file and both keys; all 13 canonical concepts are
reachable wherever a manifest declares them. The load-bearing E2E flips a
core-to-web audit from exit 1 to exit 0 by shrinking the manifest alone,
proving the manifest — not a hardcoded map — decides where rules apply.

phases.title: Resolve bindings from the manifest; delete the hardcoded maps
